data.narrative:
Dream Security, a Series B defense and security company, is evaluated against a comparables universe of 10 peers: 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms in the same sector and stage.

The stage-progression method was not applied. The current post-money valuation of $3.0B implies a step-up multiple of 1.9x to $5.7B, which exceeds 20x the company's $100M+ total raised—a threshold breach suggesting the input valuation is unreliable. The peer-median method was applicable and yielded $1.0B. The median valuation across five same-stage, same-sector peers (Harmattan AI at $1.4B, Code Metal at $1.2B, Defense Unicorns at $1.0B, Heven AeroTech at $1.0B, and TurbineOne at $300M) establishes a range of $300M to $1.4B, with a midpoint of $1.0B.

The triangulated analysis, constrained by a single applicable method, supports a valuation range of $850M to $1.1B, centered at $1.0B. Key uncertainties include reliance on a single valuation method and limited visibility into peer-company growth rates, customer concentration, and margin profiles. The wide peer range ($300M–$1.4B) also suggests meaningful heterogeneity in the cohort that a single median may not fully capture. Additional transaction or revenue multiple analysis would strengthen conviction in this range.
